newsitem.title: USA: CBS News names cult leader as Marshall Applewhite.
newsitem.headline: CBS News names cult leader as Marshall Applewhite.

text.p: The leader of the Heaven's Gate cult who led 39 people in a mass suicide in Southern California was a man named Marshall Applewhite who was questioned by police as far back as 1974, when a recruiting campaign went sour, CBS News reported on Thursday.

CBS identified Applewhite, named by the cult members on videotape as "Doe," and aired videotape from 1974 in which Applewhite spoke of rising from the dead, much as he did in a tape made just days ago and also aired on television broadcasts on Thursday.
Applewhite and his wife were arrested in Oregon in 1974 after a campaign for recruits for his cult, Higher Source, went sour, CBS said.
"Even then Marshall Applewhite was talking of rising from the dead," the network said, quoting him as predicting that he and his followers would rise from the dead in 3 1/2 days.

It also showed a tape of Applewhite made a few days ago in which he said, "You can follow us, but you cannot stay here and follow us," CBS said his body was among the 39 found dead at a mansion outside of San Diego.

CBS said the goal of Applewhite's cult was "to reach the heavens ... not heaven as organised religion which the cult disdained .... but the cosmic outerspace Hale Bopp (comet) and flying saucers. ... "
In the new tape, in which he appears with a shaved head, Applewhite, or Doe, said "You can follow us, but you cannot stay here and follow us," referring to the suicide plan.
